coach.headline: You’ve entered junctions on red
coach.pattern: In several instances you reached the stop line while the signal facing you was red, whether you were in a bike lane or the traffic lane. You then moved forward just before the light changed, even when a bus, a car or no vehicle was visible.
coach.why_it_matters: Going in on red puts you into the path of traffic that has the right of way, creating close‑call situations.
drills: Pause at every stop line, look at the signal and wait until it is green before moving.
Use the road markings as a visual cue to stop and check all directions before you cross.
Practice counting a few seconds after the light turns green to be sure it’s clear before you enter.

coach.headline: Great effort, let’s keep the bike off the pavement
coach.pattern: You frequently ride on the sidewalk when the signal ahead is not visible, alongside pedestrians and sometimes in low‑light conditions. This occurs on routes where you encounter buses, cars or motorcycles nearby, especially where a physical separator is present.
coach.why_it_matters: Sidewalk riding puts you close to foot traffic and can make drivers less aware of you, raising the chance of a near‑miss or collision.
drills: Before you start a stretch, look for a clear road or cycle lane and choose that instead of the pavement.
When you see a vehicle entrance or a bus stop ahead, shift back onto the road well before you reach it.
In dim conditions, switch on a bright front light and wear reflective gear to stay visible.

coach.headline: Watch your lane changes
coach.pattern: You were in the traffic lane and moved sideways into the path of a large vehicle that was overtaking you on the right. The truck passed very close, leaving only a narrow gap.
coach.why_it_matters: Changing line into traffic cuts the safe distance and raises the chance of a serious collision.
drills: Stay in your lane until you see a clear gap ahead.
Scan behind you before moving sideways.
Signal early and wait for at least a metre of clearance.

overview.summary: You’re making good progress but there are a few habits that need attention. By focusing on a few key changes you can ride more safely and confidently.
priorities: Avoid entering junctions when the signal facing you is red – wait for the green before moving forward
Keep the bike on the road rather than the pavement – use the road as your primary riding surface
Check the gap carefully before changing line into traffic – ensure there is enough space before shifting
overview.encouragement: Your commitment to improving your riding habits is evident and will pay off.
